Routbreak

Routbreak provides tools to quantify epidemic emergence risk in structured populations using multitype branching processes. R_ref describes the global reproduction threshold, whereas outbreak probability and R_ob depend on the population group in which infection is introduced.

The package supports Poisson and independent-edge negative-binomial offspring models, matrix diagnostics, and independent-entry Poisson–Gamma inference from early transmission data.

Installation

Routbreak is not yet available from CRAN. Install the development release from GitHub with:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("peasantxuan/Routbreak")

First analysis

Rows of R are infection destinations and columns are infection sources.

library(Routbreak)

R <- matrix(
  c(
    0.95, 0.12, 0.05,
    0.35, 0.85, 0.12,
    0.12, 0.25, 1.05
  ),
  nrow = 3,
  byrow = TRUE
)

dimnames(R) <- list(
  c("North", "Central", "Coast"),
  c("North", "Central", "Coast")
)

rob_table(R)

The returned table contains community-specific outbreak probabilities, outbreak reproduction ratios (R_ob), local and total reproduction ratios, and the common reference reproduction ratio (R_ref).

Main functions

Task Functions
Summarize epidemic risk rob_table()
Calculate individual quantities outbreak_prob(), r_ob(), r_ref(), r_local(), r_total()
Import and inspect matrices as_rmatrix(), is_irreducible(), matrix_diagnostics()
Scale or construct matrices scale_to_rref(), colocation_to_r()
Estimate a matrix infer_R(), infer_R_sufficient()
Propagate posterior uncertainty estimate_rob()

For independent-edge negative-binomial offspring, supply offspring = "nb" and the overdispersion parameter omega:

rob_table(R, offspring = "nb", omega = 0.7)

Estimation requires an explicit prior

The Poisson–Gamma inference module estimates directed matrix entries from generation-resolved transmission links or sufficient statistics. Users must provide proper Gamma shape and rate parameters. A universal per-edge prior is not supplied because its implied prior for total reproduction changes with the number of communities.

transmissions <- data.frame(
  generation = rep(1L, 4),
  source = c("A", "B", "A", "B"),
  destination = c("A", "A", "B", "B"),
  transmissions = c(12L, 4L, 3L, 16L)
)

fit <- infer_R(
  transmissions,
  initial_cases = c(A = 10, B = 20),
  prior_shape = 1,
  prior_rate = 1.6
)
fit$mle

Scalar priors apply to every non-structural edge; matrices allow edge-specific elicitation. The inference tutorial demonstrates how to start from a prior on each source’s total reproduction and allocate it across destinations.

Documentation

Start with:

  • Getting started with Routbreak
  • Function reference
  • Practical tutorial, including an age-structured Italian POLYMOD application through socialmixr

Advanced tutorials:

  • Overdispersed offspring distributions
  • Estimating outbreak reproduction ratios from early transmission data

The practical tutorial uses socialmixr’s Italian POLYMOD survey interface to estimate a 17-age-group mean contact matrix. Under an explicitly illustrative uniform per-contact transmission assumption, it transposes that matrix to Routbreak’s destination-row/source-column convention and normalizes it to R_ref = 1.5. The resulting reproduction matrix is a teaching scenario, not a directly observed estimate for an Italian epidemic. Routbreak does not copy or redistribute the POLYMOD records or the derived matrix; the website builds the example through the suggested CRAN package socialmixr. The underlying POLYMOD dataset is version 1.1, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1157934, licensed CC BY-NC 4.0.

Assumptions and unsupported regimes

Routbreak uses a fixed nonnegative reproduction matrix during the stochastic early phase. Outbreak probability is the probability of non-extinction, not a final attack rate.

Poisson r_ob() supports supercritical irreducible matrices, primitive irreducible matrices at or below threshold through the published continuation, and diagonal matrices representing independent communities. General reducible non-diagonal matrices and periodic continuation cases are reported rather than assigned an invented value. Negative-binomial r_ob() requires positive outbreak probabilities because the paper does not derive its zero-probability continuation.

Matrix inference uses an independent-entry Poisson likelihood with proper Gamma priors. It is not a negative-binomial likelihood or a structured model that fixes a normalized mixing matrix and estimates only a scalar multiplier.

Citation

The scientific framework is described in:

Wang B, Valdano E (2026). Redefining and estimating the early-phase reproduction ratio for epidemic outbreaks in spatially structured populations. PLOS Computational Biology, 22(7), e1014425. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014425

Use citation("Routbreak") for the separate package and paper citations. Routbreak does not currently have a software DOI.
